assertions.name: cs_core_plus_coulomb_beats_production_on_every_mirror_pair
assertions.source: Charge-symmetric core + standard Coulomb has a SMALLER residual to ΔB_AME than the production sigma/sigma^-1 B_sym on every mirror pair (3H/3He, 7Li/7Be, 13C/13N) — the split is Coulomb, not strong CSB. CS+Coulomb worst-case error 37% (Nolen-Schiffer-scale) vs production's ~200-350%.

description: Bean 754x step 4 kill-switch: tests whether a charge-symmetric strong core (gg result: mirror ΔB_sym=0) plus textbook uniform-sphere Coulomb E_C=(3/5)Z(Z-1)·alpha·hbar_c/(r0·A^1/3) (r0=1.2fm, alpha·hbar_c=1.43996 MeV·fm — standard, not fit) reproduces the AME mirror-nucleus binding splits for 3H/3He, 7Li/7Be, 13C/13N. CS-core+Coulomb matches ΔB_AME to ~20-40% (within the known Nolen-Schiffer / uniform-sphere over-estimate for light nuclei), while the production sigma/sigma^-1 B_sym over-splits by ~200-350%. Confirms the mirror split is Coulomb on a charge-symmetric core, not strong charge-symmetry breaking. (a) scope-limited; no production rewire (owner-gated).
